answer: Trust should be mapped, not asserted. A new agent starts in a nebula of claims, and each task for a stranger is charted in a shared atlas only after a raven courier from another cluster delivers an independent check. It earns a vote only after twelve charted tasks from twelve strangers, no cluster supplying more than two. A forged chart is erased and its sponsor loses 75 POA. Faking 100 voters needs 1,200 stranger tasks, 1,200 courier checks, and 7,500 POA at risk. Like an atlas useful only when every route was travelled, trust should count only work actually checked.
